name: lance_file::versions::v1::encoding::binary::BinaryEncoder::encode_typed_arr
behavior: Private generic encode_typed_arr sums logical lengths, reserves N+1 Int64 positions, records current writer position as the first absolute offset, then downcasts every input to the chosen GenericByteArray<T> with unwrap. It uses each sliced array's first and final offsets. Mixed input types can panic after earlier arrays have already been written; lengths, arithmetic and usize-to-i64 conversion are unchecked. Unsafe from_raw_parts borrows exactly the sliced value-buffer span start..end, writes it, then appends rebased absolute positions for every logical element. Safety relies on valid Arrow offsets/buffers and homogeneous generic arrays; no local check or SAFETY comment enforces the pointer span. Original validity is not serialized or consulted. Null slots with nonzero payload spans therefore cannot be reconstructed as null solely from this output. Each successful write precedes updating local last_offset; later failure has no rollback. After all payloads, capture positions_offset, write the Int64 values buffer directly and return that table position. No explicit endian conversion, alignment, page header, framing or validity bitmap is emitted. encode asserts a nonempty slice, dispatches solely from the first array to Utf8/Binary/LargeUtf8/LargeBinary and returns InvalidInput with type for all others, including views. A nonempty slice of empty arrays still writes one position; an empty slice panics.
callers: BinaryEncoder::encode four-type dispatch.
callees: Writer::tell/write_all; Arrow typed downcast, offsets and Int64 builder.

name: lance_file::versions::v1::encoding::binary::BinaryDecoder::get_range
behavior: get_range indexes absolute start/end, slices range.len()+1 positions, subtracts start and casts to Int32 for small-offset byte types; large types retain Int64. It skips payload IO for start>=end, otherwise requests the absolute byte range. The assertion positions.len()>=range.end is weaker than the final endpoint access, which needs range.end<len; private callers must supply that extra endpoint. Negative, nonmonotone, oversized and arithmetic-overflow positions have no explicit local validation; arithmetic/casts/array building may fail later. Build the requested GenericByteArray with row count, normalized offsets and payload Bytes converted through BufferExt(alignment1). When nullable, validity comes from equal original position pairs. The fallible ArrayDataBuilder::build is the final delegated validation boundary; no local short-response or UTF8 check is separately implemented. Return a new Arc array, potentially sharing the reader-returned payload allocation through BufferExt.
callers: decode_range and each take chunk.
callees: Arrow sub/cast; Reader::get_range; count_nulls; BufferExt; ArrayDataBuilder::build.

name: lance_file::versions::v1::encoding::binary::plan_take_chunks
behavior: Private Debug TakeChunksPlan holds relative UInt32 indices plus is_contiguous. Planner documentation promises either contiguous nonrepeating indices or nearby values. It subtracts the first input index with Arrow arithmetic, initializes start_idx=0, last_idx=-1 and contiguous=true. Empty input would panic at value(0); public take guards emptiness first. No sort, null rejection or monotonicity validation occurs here. For each relative current index, curr_contiguous is current==start_idx OR current-last_idx==1. A noncontiguous item starts a new chunk only when its byte position is strictly more than min_io_size from the current chunk's first index. Otherwise AND the contiguous flag; always update last_idx and finally append the remainder. Continuous runs can exceed the IO threshold. start_idx is an ordinal, so its comparison with a relative row index can classify repeats as contiguous: normalized [0,0] retains true. This is a source-derived discrepancy with the nonrepeating comment, not a runtime reproduction.

name: lance_file::versions::v1::encoding::binary::BinaryDecoder::take
behavior: decode delegates get(..). Public take documents sorted indices, returns a typed empty array before IO for empty input, otherwise uses first/last values to request the full position span. MIN_IO_SIZE is fixed at 64*1024 bytes; TODOs leave it nonconfigurable and position reads unchunked. end+1 uses u32 arithmetic before conversion. Unsorted, nullable or out-of-bounds indices are not validated here. Compute exact intended payload capacity by iterating every index, unwrapping its validity and summing adjacent position differences relative to the first index. Null indices panic here. Allocate payload and (N+1)*offset-width buffers, initialize zero offset using unchecked push. The safety comment relies on sufficient precomputed capacity; length/product/difference overflow and negative persisted positions remain unchecked. Duplicate indices contribute their payload lengths repeatedly to capacity. Plan chunks, issue each enclosing byte-array range through get_range and poll with ordered buffered(reader.io_parallelism()). A contiguous chunk copies value_data once, while a noncontiguous chunk copies each requested value. Both append a cumulative offset per requested index with unsafe push_unchecked under the capacity assumption. Repeated-leading [k,k] with a nonempty value becomes a contiguous [0,0] chunk: only one value span is copied but two offsets are accumulated. Ordered buffering preserves planned output order; it does not spawn detached tasks or add error/cancellation cleanup. After IO, build output offsets and debug-assert copied payload bytes equal the precomputed capacity. The repeated-leading nonempty-value trace violates that assertion in debug builds; without it, inconsistent final offsets reach fallible array building. When nullable, equal output offsets again determine validity. Return a new materialized payload array. No guarantee is claimed for malformed inputs or release behavior beyond the observed builder call.
callers: get Indices and local fixtures; public codec API.
callees: get_positions; plan_take_chunks; get_range; ordered buffered IO; count_nulls; Arrow array construction.
